contentBlocks.text: Yesterday you practiced Naam Japo. Today, the second teaching: Kirat Karo, earning an honest living through your own effort.

Kirat Karo means earning what you have through honest work — doing your own fair share of effort rather than taking shortcuts, cheating, or relying on others unfairly. For a child, this could mean truly doing your own homework instead of copying, actually practicing an instrument instead of pretending you did, or doing a chore fully instead of rushing through it. Think of one task you did recently — did you put in honest, complete effort, or did you take a shortcut? Write about one way you can practice Kirat Karo this week.
You just connected Kirat Karo to your own real life — honest effort in the things you do every day. Tomorrow we'll go deeper into the third teaching: Vand Chakko, sharing with others.

objectives: Explain Kirat Karo as earning an honest living through your own honest effort
Identify a real, age-appropriate example of practicing (or failing to practice) Kirat Karo
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's Naam Japo practice.
2. Introduce Kirat Karo, using child-appropriate examples (homework, chores, practicing an instrument).
3. Discuss honestly with the child a recent example of full effort vs. a shortcut, without shaming.
4. Complete the worksheet, writing one concrete way to practice Kirat Karo this week.
5. Preview tomorrow's topic: Vand Chakko.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just one clear example (like homework) rather than surveying multiple areas of life
Ready for more: ask them to explain why honest effort matters even when no one is watching or checking
Keep this a supportive, reflective conversation rather than a chance to scold about a specific past shortcut
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. Kirat Karo means earning what you have through honest, complete effort. 2. Examples include doing your own homework and fully completing a chore rather than rushing. 3. Answers will vary for the child's own commitment this week.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Deepens the second of the course's three named core teachings (Kirat Karo), continuing the 'one deep day per concept' pattern from Day 2's Naam Japo lesson.
